title: How Dagobert Renouf bootstrapped Logology and grew a Twitter audience from 150 to 40k
summary: Dagobert Renouf shares how he and his wife built Logology, an automated logo and brand identity tool, after two years building and two years struggling with marketing. Twitter, used to share his founder journey, became the channel that finally worked. He also covers timeboxing, slow growth and building in public.

principles.text: Build in public: sharing your founder journey on Twitter drives traffic, partnerships and customers when paid ads failed.
principles.quote: Then in the summer of 2021, I started tweeting about my journey. Eventually, I noticed more people were coming to my website, talking about my product, and recommending us to other founders.

principles.text: Make audience-building a daily habit; about 2h/day on Twitter produced 10x traffic, podcast invites and partners.
principles.quote: So I made it a part of my daily routine and now spend about 2h a day on it. Which led us to get 10x more traffic per day, being invited on 10+ podcasts, finding new partners, and so on.

principles.text: Be the public face of your company; sharing openly opens doors to customers, partners and investors.
principles.quote: You are the public face of your company and have a lot to win by connecting with the world directly.

principles.text: Start from a first-hand problem: automate an expensive service to cut price while keeping quality.
principles.quote: we looked for a way to make it cheaper without losing the quality. Eventually, we stumbled upon the idea of automating the brand research and design aspects and cut the price by 10.

principles.text: Persist through marketing failure by trying different ideas until one channel works.
principles.quote: But I didn’t want to quit and decided to keep trying different marketing ideas. And one day I found the right one (growing a Twitter audience).

principles.text: You don't need to grow fast; a slow small business that never quits can still grow every year.
principles.quote: You don’t need to go fast to succeed. All you need is to never quit.
